title: Strike Team Muster — Readiness Logbook & KPI Lattice
content:
Purpose: quick-reference logbook for the strike-team (product-ops + ops + SRE) during a high-risk rollout window. Focus: staffing rotation (muster), KPI lattice (signals -> actions), dependency backstops and minimal runbook snippets.

Audience: product ops leads, release engineers, SRE on-call, product managers owning go-live.

High-level summary:
- Goal: validate success criteria for v0.9 roll; detect regressions within 60 minutes and enable automatic/manual fallbacks.
- Primary success KPIs: 99.9% request success, p95 latency < 220ms for gen endpoints, cost per 1k tokens within target band.

KPI lattice (flat, human-readable):
KPI | Target | Alert (investigate) | Critical (action) | Owner | Action
- Availability | >= 99.9% | < 99.5% sustained 5m | < 99% or catastrophic | SRE-Leads (Jonah) | escalate -> throttles, route to backup region
- Error rate (5xx) | < 0.1% | 0.5% 5m | > 1% 3m | Serving Runtime (Miguel) | immediate canary cut / fallback to smaller model variant
- p95 latency (gen) | < 220ms | > 350ms 5m | > 600ms 3m | Infra (Hannah) | drain, scale up dedicated pool, enable cache bypass
- Token cost delta | within +-10% baseline | +10% sustained 1h | +30% 30m | Finance/ops (Asha) | enable quantized fallback, traffic shift to cheaper variant
- Quality regression (eval score) | within -2 pts baseline | -4 pts | -8 pts | Product (PM) | hold rollout, partial rollback to previous model weight

Muster schedule (T = planned rollout time):
- T-72h: alignment sync (product, eng, SRE, sales engineering) — confirm test plans + kpi baselines. Owner: Asha.
- T-48h: smoke canary in staging (internal), run 5 evaluation prompts, sanity checks. Owner: Miguel.
- T-24h: full preflight checklist (below). invite strike-team rotation. Owner: Hannah.
- T-2h: warm pools, pre-cache common prompts, lock config commits. Owner: Infra on-call.
- T: rollout start — 5% traffic canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 15m observation windows. Owner: release conductor.
- T+60m: formal readout, decision to proceed to full. T+24h: postmortem triage and kpi ledger update.

Shift roster (strike-team):
- Muster lead (single point): Asha Patel (primary), Miguel Torres (backup). Slack: #prod-readiness. Pager: on-call SRE rotation.
- Incident commander (IC): Jonah Li -> takes control of communications for critical events.
- Runtime lead: Miguel Torres -> model variant rollout decisions, kernel toggles.
- Infra lead: Hannah Kim -> autoscale, dedicated capacity, GPU pool ops.
- PM liaison: Sara Nguyen -> customer comms and product quality gating.
- Support liaison: Rajiv Patel -> triage tickets to PS/CS.

On-call split (example 12h windows):
- Day (08:00-20:00 PST): Asha (muster lead), Jonah (IC), Miguel (runtime), Hannah (infra)
- Night (20:00-08:00 PST): backup rotation (see shared shift sheet), reduced staffing but IC must be reachable.

Surge capacity plan (quick ops knobs):
1) Pre-warm: reserve 20% dedicated pool for t0->t+60. ticket JIRA-INFRA-112.
2) Autoscale threshold relax: temporarily increase target CPU/GPU headroom to 75% to avoid oscillation.
3) Batch size cap reduction: reduce max batch size by 20% if p95 latency climbs but throughput steady.
4) Cache policy: promote common prefixes to hot cache; enable KV cache for long-running chats.
Estimated incremental cost: $2.4k/day for reserved surge (notes: depends on GPU type, see cost-sim sheet).

Dependency map (critical):
- Model artifact host (S3 repo) -> owner: Models Infra (Evans). Backstop: pinned mirror in internal registry (registry-locked). Ticket: JIRA-MODEL-62.
- Tokenization microservice -> owner: Ben Carter. Fallback: local tokenizer in runtime binary (graceful degrade).
- Auth & rate limiting -> owner: Security infra. Backstop: emergency bypass token for internal calls only.
- Observability ingestion (metrics + traces) -> owner: Observability team. If metrics delayed, use log-sampling probes and lightweight heartbeat metrics.

Escalation triggers -> concise actions:
- If error-rate > 1% for 3 minutes: immediately cut canary and route new traffic to previous model tag. Notify IC, open incident.
- If p95 > 600ms for 3 minutes: enable cache-bypass on a subset, scale up serving processes, consider model-quantized fallback.
- If quality eval drops > 8 points: STOP rollout, notify customers in beta, roll back model weights.

Three short scenarios (playbooks):
1) Case: sudden error spike at 10% traffic
   - Detection: alert from error-rate rule -> Slack @strike-team.
   - First 5m: reduce traffic to 0% for canary, verify error logs, toggle model variant -> if heads-up shows NPE in transform step, revert.
   - Communication: 10m status update in #prod-readiness, notify CS for impacted customers.
   - Post-action: update incident log, assign root cause to runtime team.

2) Case: slow degradation p95 steadily rising during full traffic
   - Triage: check infra metrics (GPU utilization, host CPU, GC). If GPU memory pressure -> reduce concurrency / split jobs.
   - Action: enable warm caching, temporarily throttle some endpoints, open infra scaling ticket (JIRA-INFRA-117).

3) Case: cost bleed (token cost +40%) with stable latency and quality
   - Triage: check tokenization/formatting loop regressions in app code, look for prompt expansions.
   - Action: enable cost guard (traffic shift to cheaper quantized model at 30% of traffic), run regression eval on 50 prompts.

Minimal runbook snippets (to paste into pager duty incident):
- Canary rollback (manual):
  1) Pause new canary traffic via release console -> set canary weight = 0.
  2) Promote previous stable model tag to default routing.
  3) Repoint DNS/route if region fallback needed.
  4) Confirm end-to-end smoke tests -> mark incident status.

- Rapid fallback to cheaper model variant (automatable):
  1) Activate policy: route tier=standard -> variant=quantized-v1 for 25% of traffic.
  2) Monitor quality eval stream for 30m.
  3) If score < threshold, revert and escalate.

Preflight checklist (compact):
- [ ] Model artifact verified (checksum).
- [ ] Canary config staged and peer-reviewed.
- [ ] Stakeholders (SRE, infra, PM, CS) in call.
- [ ] Rollback plan documented + tested in dev.
- [ ] Observability dashboards pinned, synthetic probes running.
- [ ] Cost guard toggles scripted.
- [ ] Legal/compliance (if applicable) signoff completed.

Notes / TODOs / open questions:
- Q: should we include a forced read-only mode for high error severity? (open) Owner: Product.
- Q: runbook automation: who can flip quantized fallback without a full incident? (propose: infra-sre leads)
- TODO: run a 1hr surge rehearsal (simulate 2x baseline traffic) - schedule with SRE (Miguel to pick date).
- TODO: flesh out support swarming doc for CS engineers (Rajiv).

Appendix: quick links and shorthand references:
- kpi baseline sheet: CONFLUENCE-12345
- cost simulation: github.com/redwood/infra/cost-sim (PR #42)
- rollout ci job: ci/redwood-rollout-v2 (Jenkins job)

Sign-off log (iteration entries):
- 2025-02-07: initial draft by Asha (this file).
- 2025-02-20: added surge knobs + cost estimate (Hannah).
- 2025-03-04: clarified canary windows, added backup tokenization plan (Miguel).

Quick contact cheat-sheet:
- Slack: #prod-readiness (must be in channel)
- Pager: SRE primary on-call (see rota)
- War room bridge: zoom.us/j/999-888-777 (internal)

End of logbook (keep this doc living; update after every rehearsal or real rollout).
